name: K2K
summary: K2K was the first long-baseline accelerator experiment to confirm neutrino oscillation with a controlled beam, sending muon neutrinos from KEK to Super-Kamiokande.
physics_targets: Muon-neutrino disappearance at the atmospheric mass splitting
Neutrino interaction measurements with near detectors
detection_principle: Near detectors characterized the beam at KEK. Super-Kamiokande used water-Cherenkov ring reconstruction to measure the far muon-neutrino event rate and energy spectrum. The near-to-far comparison tested both event disappearance and spectral distortion.

results.summary: Observed 112 beam-originated events against 158.1 expected without oscillation, together with an energy-spectrum distortion; the no-oscillation probability was 0.0015%.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
